Read and write SDD (TDWG Structured Descriptive Data)

Source: R/sdd.R
readSDD.Rd

SDD is the XML standard of TDWG (Biodiversity Information Standards) for descriptive data: characters and their states, the taxa, and how each taxon is coded for each character. readSDD() turns an SDD file into a character matrix, writeSDD() writes one. Both follow SDD 1.1 (the http://rs.tdwg.org/UBIF/2006/ schema), which is what Lucid, Xper2/Xper3 and DELTA tools export.

Usage

readSDD(file, taxon = "Taxon", sep = "/", inapplicable = NA, dataset = NULL)

writeSDD(
  x,
  file,
  characters = NULL,
  taxon = "Taxon",
  title = NULL,
  sep = "/",
  inapplicable = NULL,
  lang = "en",
  key = NULL
)

Arguments

file

Path of the SDD file to read or write.

taxon

Name of the taxon column of the matrix.

sep

Separator between the states of a variable taxon in one cell.

inapplicable

For readers, the cell value to give "not applicable" (default NA, the same as unknown). For writers, the cell value that means "not applicable" (default NULL: none).

dataset

Which <Dataset> of the file to read, by position; by default the first one that has coded descriptions (or, for readSDDKey(), identification keys).

x

A character matrix (data frame), or the list returned by readSDD(), readDELTA(), readLucid() or readXper().

characters

Optional data frame describing the characters: a Character column matching the matrix's column names and any of Type, States (to fix the order of the states or list states no taxon has), Unit, InapplicableIf and Cost. By default taken from x if x is a reader's result; otherwise numeric columns are written as numeric characters and all others as categorical ones.

title

Title of the dataset; by default the title in the metadata of x.

lang

Language of the labels, as an xml:lang code.

key

Optional dimoose key to store in the same file as an SDD identification key (see writeSDDKey()).

Value

readSDD() returns a list of class tdwgData with

  • matrix: the character matrix;

  • characters: one row per character with Character (the column name), Type ("categorical", "ordered", "integer", "real" or "text"; SDD itself only tells categorical, real and text apart), States (all defined states, separated by sep), Unit, InapplicableIf ("Other character=state/state": the character does not apply when the other character has one of these states; several rules are separated by ;), Cost when the file has ratings, and Id;

  • taxa: Taxon, Detail and Id;

  • meta: key/value data frame (title, description, language, authors, copyright, generator, created, and keys, the number of identification keys in the file, see readSDDKey()).

writeSDD() returns file, invisibly.

The character matrix

A plain data frame with one row per taxon, the taxon names in a column (Taxon by default) and one column per character. Cells are text:

  • a state name, or several separated by sep when the taxon is variable ("red/yellow");

  • for numeric characters a value or range written the way DELTA and floras write it: "5", "2.3-7.9", "2.3-5.1-7.9" (the middle value is the mean or median) and, with rare extremes, "(1-)2-8(-12)";

  • for text characters the text;

  • NA when the character is unknown, not coded or not applicable (give inapplicable to tell "not applicable" apart).

What is read from SDD

Categorical, quantitative and text characters, in the order of the <Characters> list; the coded descriptions (<SummaryData>) of each taxon; <Status> codes (NotApplicable becomes inapplicable, the others NA); the dependency rules of the character tree (InapplicableIf, OnlyApplicableIf); and observation-convenience ratings, which become a Cost from 1 (easy) to 5. A taxon with several descriptions gets one row, with the states of all of them. States scored with a "misinterpretation" modifier (Lucid's way of catching a common mistake) are not taken as states of the taxon, and states scored with the modifier the Lucid Builder labels "unscoped" make the cell "not applicable" (the Builder defines that modifier in every SDD file it writes; none of the real exports dimoose was checked against uses it, so how it is attached to a score is assumed to be the same as for the other modifiers). Other modifiers (rarely, uncertain) are ignored and the state kept, so a character whose states are all "uncertain" for a taxon lists all of them. Dependency rules are read from the character itself and from the groups of the character tree it sits in. Quantitative measures map to the range text as follows: Min/Max are the ends of the range, unless UMethLower/UMethUpper are given too, in which case those are the normal range and Min/Max the extremes in parentheses; Mean (or Median, Mode) is the middle value. Other statistics (SD, N) are dropped.

Not read: sample data (<SampleData> of individual specimens), media, natural-language descriptions, taxon hierarchies, and text in more than one language (the first label of each object is used).

What is written

A complete, schema-valid SDD 1.1 document with the taxon names, the characters, a character tree holding the dependency rules, and one coded description per taxon. NA cells are left out (SDD reads a missing coding as unknown), cells equal to inapplicable get the status NotApplicable. A Cost from 1 to 5 is written as an observation-convenience rating, as Xper3 does. "ordered" characters are written as categorical ones and "integer" as quantitative ones, so those two types come back as "categorical" and "real". Of a cell listing several numeric ranges ("5/10-15") the overall range is written, and numbers are written as numbers ("0.40" comes back as "0.4"). A categorical character for which no taxon has a state is written as a text character, with a warning, because SDD does not allow a categorical character without states. Files written from the real datasets dimoose was tried on (DELTA, Lucid and Xper exports of up to 969 taxa) all validate against the SDD 1.1 schema; none has been imported into Lucid or Xper.

References

Hagedorn, G., Thiele, K., Morris, R. & Heidorn, P. B. (2005). Structured Descriptive Data (SDD) w3c-xml-schema, version 1.0. https://www.tdwg.org/standards/sdd/

See also

readSDDKey() for dichotomous keys stored in SDD, readXper(), readLucid(), readDELTA().

Examples

f <- system.file("extdata", "tdwg", "violets.sdd.xml", package = "dimoose")
d <- readSDD(f)
d
#> Character data "Four violets" (SDD) 
#>   4 taxa x 5 characters (3 categorical, 1 real, 1 text) 
#>   $matrix, $characters, $taxa, $meta
d$matrix
#>             Taxon Aerial stem       Flower colour     Stem hairs
#> 1   Viola odorata      absent        violet/white           <NA>
#> 2  Viola tricolor     present violet/white/yellow hairy/glabrous
#> 3   Viola biflora     present              yellow       glabrous
#> 4 Viola palustris      absent              violet           <NA>
#>     Flower length                         Notes
#> 1           13-15      Flowers strongly scented
#> 2 (10-)15-25(-30)                          <NA>
#> 3      12-13.5-15 Usually two flowers on a stem
#> 4            <NA>                          <NA>
d$characters[, c("Character", "Type", "States", "Unit")]
#>       Character        Type              States Unit
#> 1   Aerial stem categorical      present/absent     
#> 2 Flower colour categorical violet/white/yellow     
#> 3    Stem hairs categorical      hairy/glabrous     
#> 4 Flower length        real                       mm
#> 5         Notes        text                         

# write a matrix of your own
m <- data.frame(
  Taxon = c("Apis mellifera", "Bombus terrestris", "Vespula vulgaris"),
  Hair = c("sparse", "dense", "sparse/absent"),
  "Body length" = c("12-15", "(11-)14-17(-22)", NA),
  check.names = FALSE
)
chars <- data.frame(Character = "Body length", Type = "real", Unit = "mm")
out <- writeSDD(m, tempfile(fileext = ".xml"), characters = chars, title = "Three wasps and bees")
readSDD(out)$matrix
#>               Taxon          Hair     Body length
#> 1    Apis mellifera        sparse           12-15
#> 2 Bombus terrestris         dense (11-)14-17(-22)
#> 3  Vespula vulgaris sparse/absent            <NA>
